_README: Installation DATA that ships as a neutral default: which instances of each connection exist,
what each instance's secret files are called on the box, which capability needs which
connection, and the consumers that have no grants to derive their connections from. An
integration manifest (integrations/<id>/integration.json) describes the VENDOR and cannot
carry any of this, because it is the same for every installation and none of this is.
This default has ONE instance per connection and names no organisation, agent or person.
Google workspaces are not listed here at all: the console finds them from the OAuth clients
the host holds (GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID_<ORG>), and the chief of staff builds the same names from
the organisation id it is given. An installation that needs different instances edits this
file or replaces it in its own build, then regenerates.
Edit this, or an integration manifest, then run:
pnpm -C packages/agent-kit run generate:connections
That ONE command writes BOTH generated files:
packages/agent-kit/src/connections.ts         — what the console shows
packages/agent-kit/src/integration-secrets.ts — what the keeper may MOUNT
`secretEnv` on an instance is what the second one is made of: secret file name -> the
environment variable the runtime reads that file's path from. A secret with no entry is a
credential the keeper will NOT mount from an agent definition. Declare `secretEnv` on an
instance and you must declare it for EVERY secret of that instance — half a credential pair
is worse than none. An env key may appear once across the whole file.
`note` is emitted as a comment above the rendered object; `instancesNote` above its
`instances:` line; `capabilityNotes[c].above` / `.inline` around a capability's line.

connections.label: Microsoft work mailbox and calendar
note: One fixed work DATA client, separate from console sign-in.
Runtime reads require explicit personal grants and keeper-owned fixed mounts; definitions cannot choose these files.

connections.label: Google (Gmail + Calendar)
instancesNote: One OAuth client per org. Internal consent only accepts users of that client's Workspace,
which is why a user in another Workspace cannot go through another org's client. The
console lists the orgs this host holds a client for; this single entry only keeps the
connection discoverable on a blank install.

connections.label: LiteLLM gateway
note: No configEnv: GATEWAY_URL is read directly via ctx.env at each build site today, and adding
it here would change gen-compose output for no gain. Left deliberately.

connections.label: Karakeep (bookmarks)
note: Declared because the keeper mounts this key from an agent definition and no list said
so. Read by the digest schedule alongside the KARAKEEP_URL environment binding.

connections.label: Signal spine (bearer token)
note: The bearer token for the installation's own signals endpoint (SIGNAL_SPINE_URL).
Already mountable by the keeper; declared here so it is visible and rotatable like the rest.

identity.inline: reads the box's own user_aliases registry — no external credential

above: Fans out over capabilities the chief of staff already holds — so it needs their credentials, and no new one.

outside.inline: each outside tool's optional bearer token is a per-agent file the owner places on the server; the definition names the server

obligation.inline: reads/writes the box's own obligation_threads table — no external credential

note: Reads Calendar through agent-runtime's resolver, Notion with its own token, and Twenty,
for the People projection (read-only, keyed by email).
consumers.name: notion-sync
